composing_units: 4th Infantry Division; 90th Infantry Division; attached: US 82nd Airborne Division; 101st Airborne Division
engaged_with: German 709th Static Infantry Division; German 91st Luftlande Division
notes: Assault corps at Utah (Collins). 4th Div landed ~21,000 troops with 197 casualties; airborne divisions landed behind the beach.

current_activity: holding Carentan and repulsing 17th SS counterattack
notes: 101st Airborne captured Carentan 12 June (German withdrawal for lack of ammunition), joining Utah and Omaha beachheads; counter-attacked by 17th SS PzG Div 13 June.
Main westward attack taken over by 9th Division and 82nd Airborne on 14 June; Collins issued verbal orders 13 June.

current_activity: sealing off Cherbourg garrison at Barneville-sur-Mer
notes: 3rd Bn 60th Infantry (9th Div) reached Barneville-sur-Mer on 18 June, splitting German Seventh Army and sealing Cherbourg garrison; 77th Div artillery largely lost.

current_activity: attacking north toward Cherbourg on a broad front
notes: Corps attacks north on a broad front with 4th, 9th, 79th Divisions on 19 June; 90th Div and 82nd AB pass to VIII Corps same day. Storm began 19 June.
Collins launched general assault on the Cherbourg Landfront 22 June after refusal to surrender; fortified area penetrated 23–25 June; naval bombardment 25 June.

current_activity: capturing Fort du Roule; organised defence ended
notes: 79th Division captured Fort du Roule 26 June; Gen. von Schlieben captured; organised defence ended.
Deputy commander Gen. Sattler surrendered 27 June; all organised resistance in Cherbourg ceased; US engineers entered port.

current_activity: attacking Cap de la Hague; last harbour forts surrendering
notes: 9th Division attacked up the Cap de la Hague 29 June; last harbour forts surrendered same day; some holdouts to 1 July.

current_activity: opening Operation Cobra west of Saint-Lô behind the air bombardment
notes: VII Corps made the main effort of Cobra; 26 July was the second day (Breakout-13 p251). Point is the penetration sector.

location_qualifier: objective of the 26 July column; not the corps headquarters
current_activity: committing two armored columns to take Marigny and Saint-Gilles
notes: Breakout-13 p251: on 26 July Collins committed part of his reserve, two armored columns, telling one to take Marigny and the other Saint-Gilles. Batch 2 review: location_represents is objective, so the point is the named objective, not a documented position on the date (basis representative_point).

current_activity: passing the 30th Division and CCA, 2nd Armored to XIX Corps and turning south
notes: Event date: Breakout-16 p304 (by 28 July both the 30th Division and CCA of the 2nd Armored had been transferred to XIX Corps; the 22nd Infantry passed to XIX Corps; the 1st Division's 26th Infantry reinforced the 4th Division). Event definition: VII Corps loses two units and reorients from west to south for the exploitation. Location: the CMH command-post list has the corps at Marigny on 30 July, two days later. Relationship: First Army assigned. Event support: high (Green Book, 28 July). Location support: low (command post listed two days later).

current_activity: holding Mortain against the German counterattack
engaged_with: German 2nd SS Panzer Division Das Reich; German 1st SS Panzer Division Leibstandarte SS Adolf Hitler
notes: Breakout-24: 30th Division occupied Mortain on 6 August; 2nd SS Panzer attacked on 7 August with 1st SS Panzer committed north of the town.

current_activity: attacking from Melun with 3rd Armored Division through the LVIII Panzer Corps line
notes: Breakout-31 p671: 3rd Armored Division attacked from Melun on 26 August and unhinged the LVIII Panzer Corps line near Meaux.

current_activity: 3rd Armored Division taking Mons; Mons Pocket closing
notes: Breakout-32 p681: on the morning of 3 September the 3rd Armored Division took firm possession of Mons. Wikipedia credits VII Corps with about 25,000 prisoners in the Mons Pocket.

location_qualifier: objective of the VII Corps drive
current_activity: reconnaissance in force toward the Siegfried Line south of Aachen
notes: Siegfried-2 p35 maps the VII Corps breach attempt south of Aachen for 12–29 September 1944; Siegfried-4 describes the reconnaissance in force. Point is the objective area, not the corps front line. Batch 2 review: location_represents is objective, so the point is the named objective, not a documented position on the date (basis representative_point).

current_activity: 1st Division takes Aachen; the garrison commander surrenders
notes: Event date: 21 October 1944 (Siegfried p319: "21 October 1944 in Aachen, the first large German city lost in the war"; p390: "21 October, the day Aachen fell"; p315: Colonel Wilck was ready to end the fight). Event definition: the German garrison of Aachen, under Colonel Wilck, surrenders to the 26th Infantry of the VII Corps' 1st Division. The row is the city's fall, not the Aachen encirclement of 16 October. Relationship: First Army assigned. Location: Aachen city centroid; the surrender took place in a bunker inside the city, which this point does not claim to fix. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Aachen. Event support: high (dated three times in the Green Book). Location support: high for the city, low for the site inside it. Objective check: the objective was the city itself and the surrender happened in it on the row date, so documented_on_date holds.

current_activity: attacks toward the Roer after weather delays; heavy fighting at the Donnerberg and in the Hürtgen
notes: Event date: 16 November 1944 (Siegfried p528: "progress of the XIX Corps on 16 November compared favorably with that of the VII Corps, where the First Army troops had run into trouble with the Donnerberg, the Hamich ridge, and the Huertgen Forest"; p499: the XIX Corps learned before daylight on 16 November that the offensive was to begin, as did the VII Corps divisions). Event definition: the First Army's main effort (the Roer River offensive, after several postponements) opens on 16 November with VII Corps on the right of the XIX Corps; the point is the corps sector near Eschweiler and Stolberg, not a headquarters. Relationship: First Army assigned. Location: The atlas lists the corps command post at Aachen on 20 November, four days later; the point used is the sector centre near Eschweiler, not the Aachen command post. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Eschweiler. Event support: high (Green Book narrative). Location support: low (a representative sector point; no command post is listed for 16 November). Location support fallback: coordinates are a sector point; location_date records the nearest command-post entry only for orientation.

composing_units: 84th Infantry Division; 2nd Armored Division; 75th Infantry Division
current_activity: officially assumes its Ardennes front at 1630 with the 84th Division in the centre
notes: Event date: 23 December 1944 (Ardennes p433: "The new corps front (officially assumed by the VII Corps at 1630 on 23 December) would reach from the Ourthe River on the left to the junction of the Lesse and Meuse on the right, approximately fifty miles"; p432: on the 22nd Collins and some corps troops moved into the new area southwest of Liège). Event definition: the VII Corps takes over its Ardennes front, with the 84th Infantry Division already holding the centre, the 2nd Armored Division closing to the rear and the 75th Infantry Division in reserve; the 3rd Armored Division is still the right wing of the XVIII Airborne Corps (p432). The row exists to date the end of the XVIII Airborne Corps' control of the 84th Division (C0560): the CMH table lists VII Corps for the 84th from 20 December, but the Green Book has the XVIII Airborne Corps still giving the division orders on 21 and 22 December. Relationship: First Army assigned (C0530); the corps is under 21st Army Group's operational control through First Army from 20 December (C0520). Location: the atlas lists the corps command post at Durbuy on 23 December. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Durbuy. Event support: high (an hour is given by the Green Book). Location support: moderate (an atlas entry for the date; the Green Book does not name the place).
